'''Chris Q Doe''' (Born 1958) is a professor of Biology,<ref>{{cite web|title=Chris Doe {{!}} Institute of Neuroscience|url=http://ion.uoregon.edu/content/chris-doe-0|website=ion.uoregon.edu|language=en}}</ref> and [[Howard Hughes Medical Institute]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Chris Q. Doe, PhD {{!}} HHMI.org|url=http://www.hhmi.org/scientists/chris-q-doe|website=HHMI.org|language=en}}</ref> investigator at the Institute for Neuroscience, [[University of Oregon]], [[Eugene, Oregon]], United States. Doe did his PhD work with [[Corey Goodman]] at [[Stanford University]], followed by postdoctoral fellowship with [[Matthew P. Scott]] at [[University of Colorado Boulder]]. He is a researcher in [[developmental biology]] known for his studies on [[neurogenesis]] in [[Drosophila melanogaster]] [[neural stem cell]] [[neuroblast]]s.<ref>{{cite web|title=cq doe - Google Scholar Citations|url=https://scholar.google.co.uk/citations?user=QyzLq4YAAAAJ&hl=en&authuser=1|website=scholar.google.co.uk}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Doe|first1=CQ|last2=Goodman|first2=CS|title=Early events in insect neurogenesis. II. The role of cell interactions and cell lineage in the determination of neuronal precursor cells.|journal=Developmental Biology|date=September 1985|volume=111|issue=1|pages=206–19 |pmid=4029507|doi=10.1016/0012-1606(85)90446-4}}</ref> His lab investigates the generation of neuronal diversity and neural circuit formation in [[Drosophila melanogaster]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Home|url=http://www.doelab.org/|website=www.doelab.org}}</ref> Doe is also a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|title=National Academy of Sciences members 2017|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-2-2017-NAS-Election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170503160816/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-2-2017-NAS-Election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 3, 2017}}</ref>
